title: Real-Time Collaborative Code Editor & Runner
shortDescription: Browser-based collaborative IDE supporting multi-user concurrent code editing via Operational Transformation (CRDT / Yjs), real-time WebSockets, Monaco Editor, and containerized code execution.
problemStatement: Engineering teams and technical interviewers require synchronized, zero-latency code sharing where multiple developers edit the same file simultaneously without keystroke clobbering, race conditions, or editor desynchronization.
objectives: Integrate Microsoft Monaco Editor into a React TypeScript interface supporting syntax highlighting for 10+ languages.
Implement real-time bidirectional synchronization over WebSockets with room isolation so each collaborative session remains private.
Resolve concurrent text edit conflicts gracefully using CRDTs (Conflict-Free Replicated Data Types).
Provide a secure code execution sandbox evaluating Python, JavaScript, and C++ code with strict timeout limits.
realWorldUseCase: Live technical interview platforms (similar to CoderPad / HackerRank), remote pair-programming tools, and interactive computer science classroom environments.

architecture.overview: React client hosts the Monaco Editor connected via WebSocket to a Node.js signaling cluster. Text mutations are structured as Yjs CRDT operations, eliminating central conflict resolution bottlenecks. Redis Pub/Sub synchronizes messages across multiple Node.js socket server instances. A decoupled sandbox worker executes user-submitted code in disposable, resource-constrained Docker containers.

features: Sub-50ms peer-to-peer keystroke synchronization using CRDT operational transforms.
Remote user cursor markers displaying peer username and cursor selections in real time.
Isolated room codes with password protection and link-sharing invites.
Sandboxed code runner evaluating Python 3 and Node.js with output capture and error reporting.
Customizable themes (Dark / Light) with font sizing and language mode toggles.

interviewQuestions.question: What is the difference between WebSockets and standard HTTP REST polling?
interviewQuestions.answer: HTTP REST is unidirectional and request-driven: the client must continuously poll the server to discover updates, creating high HTTP header overhead and latency. WebSockets maintain a persistent, bidirectional, full-duplex TCP connection, allowing the server to push text mutations to clients in microseconds with minimal framing overhead.

interviewQuestions.question: What is a CRDT (Conflict-Free Replicated Data Type), and how does it prevent text corruption?
interviewQuestions.answer: A CRDT is a distributed data structure that guarantees eventual consistency across multiple nodes without requiring a central coordinator. Unlike naive Operational Transformation (OT) which requires complex server transformation matrices, CRDTs assign unique fractional identifiers and vector timestamps to every character inserted or deleted, ensuring all clients converge to the exact same text state regardless of packet arrival order.

interviewQuestions.question: How did you prevent users from executing malicious code (like 'rm -rf /') in the code runner?
interviewQuestions.answer: User code is never executed directly on the host operating system. It executes inside ephemeral Docker containers running with non-root user privileges, a read-only root filesystem, disabled network access (`--net=none`), CPU quotas (`--cpus=0.5`), memory limits (`--memory=128m`), and a strict process timeout kill signal.

faqs.question: Can this project be hosted for free during portfolio demonstrations?
faqs.answer: Yes. The Next.js/React frontend can be deployed on Vercel, and the Node.js WebSocket backend can be hosted on free tiers of Render or Railway.
